NEW YORK--(BUSINESS WIRE)--American Strategic Investment Co. (NYSE: NYC) (“ASIC” or the “Company”), a company that owns a portfolio of commercial real estate located within the five boroughs of New York City, announced today its financial and operating results for the third quarter ended September 30, 2026.

Third Quarter 2026 Highlights

  • Revenue was $7.1 million compared to $12.3 million in the third quarter of 2025, primarily related to the disposition of 1140 Avenue of the Americas in the prior year
  • Net loss attributable to common stockholders was $6.7 million, compared to net income of $35.8 million in the third quarter of 2025 that was primarily due to a non-cash gain recognized in connection with the disposition of 1140 Avenue of the Americas in the third quarter of 2025
  • Cash net operating income (“Cash NOI”) was $3.5 million, compared to $5.3 million in the third quarter of 2025
  • Adjusted EBITDA was $1.0 million, compared to $1.9 million in the third quarter of 2025
  • Weighted-average remaining lease term(1) was 6.0 years compared to 6.1 years at the end of the second quarter of 2026
  • 69% of annualized straight-line rent from top 10 tenants(2) was derived from investment grade or implied investment grade(3) rated tenants with a weighted-average remaining lease term of 6.7 years, up slightly from 6.4 years at the end of the prior quarter
  • Portfolio comprised of fixed rate debt at a 4.56% weighted-average interest rate
  • Subsequent to quarter end, signed an extension and expansion lease with the State of New York at 123 William Street extending the current lease to 2037 and adding approximately 30,000 square feet on two additional floors.

CEO Comments

“The Company’s results this quarter build on the progress we made over the last two quarters, as our capital prioritization strategy continues to contribute to our results,” said Nicholas Schorsch, Jr., CEO of ASIC. “The portfolio’s high quality, largely investment grade tenant base continues to support stable performance this year. We remain focused on completing our remaining asset dispositions and directing capital toward the opportunities we believe will create the most durable value for our shareholders, such as the execution of the lease with the State of New York after the end of the quarter that increases pro-forma occupancy at 123 William Street to approximately 75% and portfolio occupancy to approximately 78%.”

Real Estate Portfolio

The Company’s portfolio consisted of five properties comprised of 0.7 million rentable square feet (excluding our 1140 Avenue of the Americas property, which is in a consensual foreclosure process) as of September 30, 2026. Portfolio metrics include:

  • 74.0% leased
  • 6.0 years remaining weighted-average lease term
  • 69% of annualized straight-line rent(4) from top 10 tenants derived from investment grade or implied investment grade tenants with 6.7 years of weighted-average remaining lease term
  • Diversified portfolio, comprised of 28% government and public administration tenants, 15% retail tenants, 12% non-profit, 11% fitness and 34% all other industries, based on annualized straight-line rent

Capital Structure and Liquidity Resources

As of September 30, 2026, the Company had $5.3 million of cash and cash equivalents(5). The Company’s net debt(6) to gross asset value(7) was 58.6%, with net debt of $245.7 million.

All of the Company’s debt was fixed-rate as of September 30, 2026. The Company’s total combined debt had a weighted-average interest rate of 4.56%(8).

Advisor Payments Made with Common Stock Issuances in Lieu of Cash

In furtherance of the Company's ongoing strategy to prioritize and preserve operating capital, in August 2026 the Company’s external advisor (the “Advisor”) elected to receive shares of the Company’s Class A common stock in lieu of $1,122,149 in advisory fees accrued and payable through August 2026 under the Company’s second amended and restated advisory agreement with the Advisor (the “Advisory Agreement”). The election was approved by the Compensation Committee of the Company’s Board of Directors. Additionally, on October 23, 2026, the Company issued 244,480 shares in lieu of $1,410,651 in cash for asset management and property management services accrued and payable through October 2026. The Company has previously issued shares of its Class A common stock in lieu of cash to the Advisor and the Company’s property manager as part of its ongoing efforts to manage operating expenses and conserve liquidity.

Subsequent Events

New York State Lease Signed at 123 William Street

On November 3, 2026 the Company completed a new 11-year lease at its property at 123 William Street. The State of New York, an existing tenant, signed the lease which expanded their presence in the building to 70,629 square feet.

400 E. 67th Street/200 Riverside Blvd. Foreclosure Litigation

For a discussion of the foreclosure litigation initiated as a result of alleged defaults under the loan agreement governing the indebtedness secured by the 400 E. 67th Street and 200 Riverside Blvd. properties, see Note 5 — Mortgage Notes Payable, Net — Debt Covenant Non-Compliance, Cash Sweep Events, Notices of Defaults and of Acceleration and Foreclosure Litigation to the Company’s condensed consolidated financial statements included in its Quarterly Report on Form 10-Q for the quarter ended September 30, 2026.

Notes Payable to Related Parties

Pursuant to the terms of a promissory note executed during the fourth quarter between the Company and the Advisor, the Company borrowed $0.3 million from the Advisor for working capital needs. The promissory note bore interest at an annual rate of 8.15% and would have been callable on or after January 21, 2027. Amounts repaid under the promissory note may not be reborrowed. During the fourth quarter of 2026, the Company repaid all amounts outstanding under this promissory note with the Advisor with cash on hand including interest, which was immaterial.

Non-GAAP Financial Measures

This release discusses the non-GAAP financial measures we use to evaluate our performance, including Earnings before Interest, Taxes, Depreciation and Amortization (“EBITDA”), Adjusted Earnings before Interest, Taxes, Depreciation and Amortization (“Adjusted EBITDA”), Net Operating Income (“NOI”) and Cash Net Operating Income (“Cash NOI”) and Cash Paid for Interest. A description of these non-GAAP measures and reconciliations to the most directly comparable GAAP measure, which is net loss, is provided above.

In December 2022 we announced that we changed our business strategy and terminated our election to be taxed as a REIT effective January 1, 2023, however, our business and operations have not materially changed in the third quarter of 2026. Therefore, we did not change any of the non-GAAP metrics that we have historically used to evaluate performance.

Caution on Use of Non-GAAP Measures

EBITDA, Adjusted EBITDA, NOI, Cash NOI and Cash Paid for Interest should not be construed to be more relevant or accurate than the current GAAP methodology in calculating net income or in its applicability in evaluating our operating performance. The method utilized to evaluate the value and performance of real estate under GAAP should be construed as a more relevant measure of operational performance and considered more prominently than the non-GAAP metrics.

As a result, we believe that the use of these non-GAAP metrics, together with the required GAAP presentations, provide a more complete understanding of our performance, including relative to our peers and a more informed and appropriate basis on which to make decisions involving operating, financing, and investing activities. However, these non-GAAP metrics are not indicative of cash available to fund ongoing cash needs, including the ability to pay cash dividends. Investors are cautioned that these non-GAAP metrics should only be used to assess the sustainability of our operating performance excluding these activities, as they exclude certain costs that have a negative effect on our operating performance during the periods in which these costs are incurred.

Adjusted Earnings before Interest, Taxes, Depreciation and Amortization, Net Operating Income, Cash Net Operating Income and Cash Paid for Interest.

We believe that EBITDA and Adjusted EBITDA, which is defined as earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization adjusted for (i) impairment charges, (ii) interest income or other income or expense, (iii) gains or losses on debt extinguishment, (iv) equity-based compensation expense, (v) acquisition and transaction costs, (vi) gains or losses from the sale of real estate investments and (vii) expenses paid with issuances of common stock in lieu of cash is an appropriate measure of our ability to incur and service debt. We consider EBITDA and Adjusted EBITDA useful indicators of our performance. Because these metrics’ calculations exclude such factors as depreciation and amortization of real estate assets, interest expense, and equity-based compensation (which can vary among owners of identical assets in similar conditions based on historical cost accounting and useful-life estimates), these metrics; presentations facilitate comparisons of operating performance between periods and between other companies that use these measures. Adjusted EBITDA should not be considered as an alternative to cash flows from operating activities, as a measure of our liquidity or as an alternative to net income as an indicator of our operating activities. Other companies may calculate Adjusted EBITDA differently and our calculation should not be compared to that of other companies.

NOI is a non-GAAP financial measure used by us to evaluate the operating performance of our real estate. NOI is equal to total revenues, excluding contingent purchase price consideration, less property operating and maintenance expense. NOI excludes all other items of expense and income included in the financial statements in calculating net income (loss). We believe NOI provides useful and relevant information because it reflects only those income and expense items that are incurred at the property level and presents such items on an unleveraged basis. We use NOI to assess and compare property level performance and to make decisions concerning the operations of the properties. Further, we believe NOI is useful to investors as a performance measure because, when compared across periods, NOI reflects the impact on operations from trends in occupancy rates, rental rates, operating expenses and acquisition activity on an unleveraged basis, providing perspective not immediately apparent from net income (loss). NOI excludes certain items included in calculating net income (loss) in order to provide results that are more closely related to a property’s results of operations. For example, interest expense is not necessarily linked to the operating performance of a real estate asset. In addition, depreciation and amortization, because of historical cost accounting and useful life estimates, may distort operating performance at the property level. NOI presented by us may not be comparable to NOI reported by other companies that define NOI differently. We believe that in order to facilitate a clear understanding of our operating results, NOI should be examined in conjunction with net income (loss) as presented in our consolidated financial statements. NOI should not be considered as an alternative to net income (loss) as an indication of our performance or to cash flows as a measure of our liquidity or our ability to pay dividends.

Cash NOI, is a non-GAAP financial measure that is intended to reflect the performance of our properties. We define Cash NOI as NOI excluding amortization of above/below market lease intangibles and straight-line adjustments that are included in GAAP lease revenues. We believe that Cash NOI is a helpful measure that both investors and management can use to evaluate the current financial performance of our properties and it allows for comparison of our operating performance between periods and to other companies. Cash NOI should not be considered as an alternative to net income, as an indication of our financial performance, or to cash flows as a measure of liquidity or our ability to fund all needs. The method by which we calculate and present Cash NOI may not be directly comparable to the way other companies present Cash NOI.

Cash Paid for Interest is calculated based on the interest expense less non-cash portion of interest expense and amortization of mortgage (discount) premium, net. Management believes that Cash Paid for Interest provides useful information to investors to assess our overall solvency and financial flexibility. Cash Paid for Interest should not be considered as an alternative to interest expense as determined in accordance with GAAP or any other GAAP financial measures and should only be considered together with and as a supplement to our financial information prepared in accordance with GAAP.

Key Terms

straight-line rentfinancial
An accounting method that spreads the total rent cost or rental income evenly across the full lease period, so each reporting period shows the same amount even if actual cash payments vary (for example, due to free months or stepped increases). For investors, straight-line rent matters because it smooths earnings and can hide timing differences between cash flow and reported profit, affecting measures like operating income and the apparent stability of a landlord’s or tenant’s finances—think of turning a lumpy payment schedule into a steady monthly subscription on the books.
consensual foreclosurefinancial
A consensual foreclosure is the enforcement of a lender’s security interest in collateral that the borrower agreed in advance could be seized or sold if certain contract conditions (typically a default) occur. It relies on a prior agreement—such as a mortgage, deed of trust, or security agreement—that authorizes the lender to take possession, sell the asset, or otherwise satisfy the debt, and it may proceed under a nonjudicial process specified by the contract and applicable statute or by judicial sale if required. The key distinction is that the borrower previously granted the remedy in the security instrument, so the foreclosure enforces those agreed remedies rather than arising from an unrelated court judgment against the debtor.
promissory notefinancial
A promissory note is a written IOU in which one party promises to pay a specific sum, often with interest, to another party by a set date or on demand. Investors care because it functions like a loan: it creates a legal claim on future cash flows, carries credit and timing risk, and can affect valuation or liquidity—think of it as a formal, tradable promise to be repaid that can be assessed like any other debt investment.

NEW YORK, Nov. 13, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- SkyAI, Inc. (Nasdaq: SKYA) (“SkyAI” or the “Company”) today announced the preliminary results of its previously announced cash tender offer (the “Offer”) to purchase shares of its common stock and certain outstanding warrants. The Offer expired at one minute after 11:59 p.m., New York City time, on November 12, 2026.

Based on the preliminary count by MacKenzie Partners, Inc., the depositary and information agent for the Offer (the “Depositary”) and in accordance with the terms and conditions of the Offer, SkyAI expects to purchase the following securities validly tendered and not validly withdrawn prior to the expiration of the Offer:

  • Common stock: Approximately 47.0 million shares at $3.00 per share.
  • Pre-funded warrants: Approximately 5.1 million cash pre-funded warrants and 10.5 million cryptocurrency pre-funded warrants at $3.00 per warrant less the $0.0001 exercise price.
  • Strategic warrants: Approximately 3.9 million strategic warrants at $3.00 per warrant less the $0.0001 exercise price.
  • Stapled warrants: Approximately 34.5 million cash stapled warrants and 21.5 million cryptocurrency stapled warrants at $0.17 per warrant.

The aggregate purchase price is expected to be approximately $209 million, excluding fees and expenses related to the Offer.

The number of securities expected to be purchased by SkyAI is preliminary and subject to change. The preliminary information contained in this press release is subject to confirmation by the Depositary. The final number of securities to be purchased by SkyAI will be announced following completion of the Depositary's confirmation process. Payment for securities accepted for purchase under the Offer will occur promptly in accordance with the terms of the Offer.

About SkyAI

SkyAI, Inc. (Nasdaq: SKYA) is an artificial intelligence company building an agentic finance platform for the Global South. For additional information, please visit https://www.skyai.co/.

Millicom (Tigo) signs agreement to acquire Entel Peru, expanding its presence across Latin America

The transaction expands Millicom’s presence in investment-grade markets and is expected to be accretive to equity free cash flow in the first year following completion. Closing is expected in early December, subject to customary closing conditions.

  

Luxembourg, November 13, 2026 – Millicom (NASDAQ: TIGO) today announced that it has signed an agreement to acquire Entel Peru for US$1,714 million, including lease liabilities, implying a transaction multiple of 5.0x estimated 2026 EBITDA, before synergies and integration costs. This transaction marks another important step in Millicom's regional growth strategy and is expected to be funded through a combination of local financing and cash on hand. The purchase price will be paid in three installments: 65% at closing, 10% twelve months after closing, and 25% eighteen months after closing. The transaction is expected to close in early December 2026, subject to satisfaction of certain closing conditions.

Upon completion, the acquisition would expand Millicom’s footprint to 13 markets and further advance its strategy of geographic diversification, increasing its presence in investment-grade economies. Peru, which holds investment-grade sovereign ratings from Moody’s, S&P and Fitch, offers a market of more than 34 million people and an attractive foundation for long-term growth in connectivity and digital services.

Entel Peru’s established network, strong postpaid customer base and enterprise relationships provide an attractive platform for profitable growth. Following completion, Millicom intends to build on these strengths by applying its operational improvement capabilities, regional purchasing power and disciplined approach to capital allocation. The Group sees significant opportunities to improve efficiency, optimize working capital and strengthen cash generation, while preserving service quality and customer experience.

The acquisition would also create opportunities to expand higher-value services for consumers and businesses. Entel Peru’s access to an extensive fiber footprint through wholesale partnerships, combined with Millicom’s experience in mobile and home connectivity, would support capital-efficient growth in convergent services, stronger customer relationships and additional recurring revenues.

Millicom expects the transaction to be accretive to equity free cash flow in its first year following completion, consistent with the approach taken in its recent Telefónica acquisitions. Despite the anticipated closing late in the year, the Group expects year-end 2026 leverage to remain around 2.5x, including the acquisition. The transaction is not expected to adversely affect planned shareholder distributions and is expected to strengthen the Group’s capacity to support distributions over time through increased cash generation.

Marcelo Benitez, CEO of Millicom, commented: “We are very excited about entering Peru, a great country with tremendous potential and an important new chapter in our growth journey across Latin America. Over the past few years, we have demonstrated our ability to successfully integrate new operations, improve customer experience and deliver strong financial results. We have a proven playbook built around our Double-E strategy: delivering the best customer Experience with the greatest Efficiency. We are confident in our ability to replicate that success in Peru. Entel Peru brings a strong network, loyal customers and a talented team. Together, we see a great opportunity to invest in connectivity, bring better services and greater value to Peruvian consumers and businesses, and contribute to the country’s digital development. Our focus remains the same: disciplined execution, profitable growth and sustainable cash flow generation. We look forward to welcoming the Entel Peru team to the Millicom family and building a successful future together.”

Peru: An attractive platform for long-term growth

  • A sizeable market with significant digital potential: With more than 34 million people, Peru offers a substantial customer base for mobile connectivity, home broadband and enterprise solutions. Millicom sees opportunities to deepen digital adoption and expand higher-value services for households and businesses.
  • A growing economy with an attractive medium-term outlook: The IMF’s October 2026 projections anticipate economic growth of 2.9% in 2027 and 3.2% in 2028, with nominal GDP reaching approximately US$414 billion in 2027. Strong macroeconomic institutions, relatively low public debt and substantial international reserves provide a supportive foundation for long-term investment.
  • Investment-grade credentials and international investor confidence: Peru holds investment-grade sovereign ratings of Baa1 from Moody’s, BBB from Fitch and BBB− from S&P. As of November 5, 2026, its J.P. Morgan sovereign bond spread stood at 121 basis points, approximately 43% below the Latin American benchmark, placing Peru among the region’s lowest sovereign-risk markets.
  • Growing demand for recurring connectivity services: Mobile service revenues increased by 5.6% and fixed internet revenues by 5.8% in 2025, according to OSIPTEL. Postpaid and controlled-plan mobile subscriptions grew by 10.1%, highlighting an expanding market for recurring services and deeper customer relationships.
  • Expanding fiber adoption across the country: Fiber connections grew by approximately 21% in 2025, with growth exceeding 26% outside Lima and Callao. This expansion supports opportunities to combine mobile and home broadband services, improve customer retention and bring advanced connectivity to more communities.
  • A strong fit with Millicom’s capabilities: These market dynamics offer an attractive setting for Millicom to apply its regional scale, experience in convergent services and disciplined investment approach. Following completion, the Group would seek to translate this potential into profitable growth, stronger cash generation and lasting benefits for customers.

Nasdaq Listing Rule 5550(a)(2) requires listed securities to maintain a minimum bid price of US$1.00 per share, and Nasdaq Listing Rule 5810(c)(3)(A) provides that a failure to meet the minimum bid price requirement exists if the deficiency continues for a period of 30 consecutive business days. Based on the closing bid price of the Company's Class A ordinary shares for the 30 consecutive business days from September 29, 2026 to November 9, 2026, the Company no longer meets the minimum bid price requirement.

The Notification Letter does not impact the Company's listing on the Nasdaq Capital Market at this time. In accordance with Nasdaq Listing Rule 5810(c)(3)(A), the Company has been provided 180 calendar days, or until May 10, 2027, to regain compliance with Nasdaq Listing Rule 5550(a)(2). To regain compliance, the Company's Class A ordinary shares must have a closing bid price of at least US$1.00 for a minimum of 10 consecutive business days. In the event the Company does not regain compliance by May 10, 2027, the Company may be eligible for additional time to regain compliance or may face delisting.

The Company's business operations are not affected by the receipt of the Notification Letter. The Company intends to monitor the closing bid price of its Class A ordinary shares and may, if appropriate, consider implementing available options, including, but not limited to, implementing a share consolidation, to regain compliance with the minimum bid price requirement under the Nasdaq Listing Rules.

HOUSTON--(BUSINESS WIRE)--

ECA MARCELLUS TRUST I (OTCID Basic Market: ECTM) announced today that the Trust’s distribution for the quarter ended September 30, 2026, will be $0.021 per unit, which is expected to be distributed on or before November 30, 2026, to holders of record as of the close of business on November 23, 2026.

Since the first quarter of 2019, the Trustee has been gradually building a cash reserve for the payment of future known, anticipated or contingent expenses or liabilities of the Trust by withholding cash reserve amounts from each quarterly distribution. In November 2021, the Trustee notified Greylock Energy LLC that the Trustee had determined to increase the targeted cash reserve from the initially stated amount of approximately $1.8 million, to approximately $3.8 million. From the first quarter of 2019 through the fourth quarter of 2022, the Trustee withheld an amount from each distribution equal to the greater of $90,000 or 10% of the funds otherwise available for distribution each quarter. Since achieving the initial target of $1.8 million in the quarter ended December 31, 2022, the Trustee has been withholding, and currently plans to continue to withhold, $90,000 per quarter until a total of approximately $3.8 million in cash reserves is withheld. The Trustee may increase or decrease the targeted amount at any time and may increase or decrease the rate at which it is withholding funds to build the cash reserve at any time, without advance notice to the unitholders. Cash held in reserve will be invested as required by the trust agreement. Any cash reserved in excess of the amount necessary to pay or provide for the payment of future known, anticipated or contingent expenses or liabilities of the Trust eventually will be distributed to unitholders, together with interest earned on the funds. The Trustee has elected to withhold approximately $90,000 this quarter.

The Trust was formed to own royalty interests in natural gas properties now held by Greylock Energy LLC and certain of its wholly owned subsidiaries (“Greylock”) in the Marcellus Shale formation in Greene County, Pennsylvania. The Trust is entitled to receive certain amounts of the proceeds attributable to Greylock’s interest in the sale of production from the properties. As described in the Trust's filings, the amount of the quarterly distributions is expected to fluctuate from quarter to quarter, depending on the proceeds received by the Trust as a result of production and natural gas prices and the amount of the Trust's administrative expenses, among other factors. The amount of proceeds received or expected to be received by the Trust (and its ability to pay distributions) has been and will continue to be directly affected by the volatility in commodity prices, which are subject to a variety of factors that are beyond the control of the Trust or Greylock. Low natural gas prices will reduce proceeds to which the Trust is entitled, which will reduce the amount of cash available for distribution to unitholders and in certain periods could result in no distributions to unitholders.

Pursuant to Section 1446 of the Internal Revenue Code of 1986 (the “IRC”), withholding tax on income effectively connected to a United States trade or business allocated to non-U.S. persons (“ECI”) should be made at the highest marginal rate. Under IRC Section 1441, withholding tax on fixed, determinable, annual, periodic income from United States sources allocated to non-U.S. persons should be made at a 30% rate unless the rate is reduced by treaty. Nominees and brokers should withhold at the highest marginal rate on the distribution made to non-U.S. persons. A non-U.S. holder’s gain on the sale of Trust units is treated as ECI to the extent such holder would have had ECI if the Trust had sold all of its assets at fair market value on the date of the sale or exchange. A transferee of units is also required to withhold 10% of the amount realized on the sale or exchange of units (generally, the purchase price) unless the transferor certifies that it is not a nonresident alien individual or foreign corporation, or other exception is available. BARCELONA, Spain, Nov. 13, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Freightos Limited (NASDAQ: CRGO) ("Freightos" or the "Company"), the leading vendor-neutral global freight pricing, booking and procurement platform, today announced that on November 10, 2026, it received a written notification letter (the "Notification Letter") from the Listing Qualifications Department of The Nasdaq Stock Market LLC ("Nasdaq") notifying the Company that it is not in compliance with the minimum bid price requirement set forth in Nasdaq Listing Rule 5550(a)(2) for continued listing on the Nasdaq Capital Market.

Nasdaq Listing Rule 5550(a)(2) requires listed securities to maintain a minimum bid price of $1.00 per share, and Nasdaq Listing Rule 5810(c)(3)(A) provides that a failure to meet this requirement exists if the deficiency continues for a period of 30 consecutive business days. The Notification Letter indicated that the closing bid price of the Company's ordinary shares had been below $1.00 per share for 30 consecutive business days, from September 29, 2026 through November 9, 2026.

Compliance Period

In accordance with Nasdaq Listing Rule 5810(c)(3)(A), the Company has been provided an initial period of 180 calendar days from the date of the Notification Letter, or until May 10, 2027, to regain compliance with the minimum bid price requirement. The Company will regain compliance if, at any time during this compliance period, the closing bid price of its ordinary shares is at least $1.00 per share for a minimum of 10 consecutive business days, unless Nasdaq exercises its discretion to extend this period under Nasdaq Listing Rule 5810(c)(3)(H). If the Company regains compliance, Nasdaq will provide the Company with written confirmation and the matter will be closed.

If the Company does not regain compliance by May 10, 2027, the Company may be eligible for an additional 180-calendar-day compliance period.  

No Immediate Effect on Listing

The Notification Letter has no immediate effect on the listing of the Company's ordinary shares. The Company's ordinary shares will continue to be listed and to trade on the Nasdaq Capital Market under the symbol "CRGO" during the compliance period. The Notification Letter does not affect the Company's business operations.

The Company intends to monitor the closing bid price of its ordinary shares and is evaluating available options to regain compliance with the minimum bid price requirement within the applicable compliance period, which may include, if necessary, effecting a reverse share split, subject to any required shareholder approval. There can be no assurance that the Company will regain compliance with the minimum bid price requirement or maintain compliance with any other Nasdaq continued listing requirement.

Revenue for the First Nine Months of 2026 Surged 382.1% Year-on-Year to Approximately $9.6 Million

Profit Turnaround for the First Nine Months of 2026 with Net Income of $3.6 Million

OSAKA, Japan, Nov. 13, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- FiEE, Inc. (NASDAQ:FIEE) ("FiEE," the "Company," "we," "our," or similar terms), a technology company that leverages IoT, connectivity, and AI to deliver SaaS solutions for content creation and brand management, along with phygital art advisory services that connect artists, collectors, and brands, today announced its unaudited financial results for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026.

Operational and Financial Highlights for the Nine Months Ended September 30, 2026

  • Revenue surged 382.1% year-on-year to approximately $9.6 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, compared to $2.0 million in the same period of 2025. The increase in revenue primarily reflects the Company's strategic transition from legacy hardware operations to SaaS solutions, with a new business model focusing on integrating AI and big data into content creation and brand management, along with the successful expansion into multiple new business lines, including SaaS – MCN digital services, software services, phygital art advisory services (currently, digital authentication services), and other services, most of which experienced rapid growth following their launch.
    • As of September 30, 2026, FiEE had onboarded 939 customers for its SaaS – MCN digital services, representing total service fees of $9.2 million, of which $9.0 million had been recognized as revenue on a cumulative basis. During the nine months ended September 30, 2026, we recognized $3.7 million in revenue from this business.
    • As of September 30, 2026, FiEE had secured contracts totaling $4.1 million for software services. We recognized $2.3 million in software services revenue during the nine months ended September 30, 2026, under the applicable over-time or point-in-time revenue recognition model. The number of software services customers increased by one from June 30, 2026, bringing the total to 32 as of September 30, 2026.
    • For the nine months ended September 30, 2026, the Company's phygital art advisory services generated revenue of $3.5 million, compared to $0 for the same period in 2025. These services had served a total of five corporate clients and 601 individual clients, with related accounts receivable of $2.2 million.
  • Gross profit was approximately $7.3 million, compared to $1.6 million in the same period of 2025. The increase in gross profit was attributable to higher revenue during the period. Gross margin decreased to 76.3% for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, from 83.0% in the same period of 2025. The expansion of our MCN digital services, software services, and phygital art advisory services has changed our revenue mix and cost structure, while higher amortization costs included in cost of revenues also contributed to the decrease in consolidated gross margin during the period.
  • Net income was approximately $3.6 million, representing a turnaround from a net loss of $1.3 million in the same period of 2025.

Operational and Financial Highlights for the Three Months Ended September 30, 2026

  • Revenue was approximately $2.6 million, compared to $1.9 million for the three months ended September 30, 2025.
  • Gross profit was approximately $1.9 million, compared to $1.6 million for the three months ended September 30, 2025.
  • Net income was approximately $1.1 million, representing a turnaround from a net loss of $0.3 million for the three months ended September 30, 2025.

Rafael Li, Chief Executive Officer and President of FiEE, commented, "We delivered solid financial results during the period and made meaningful progress in building a more diversified, scalable digital services platform. By expanding our AI-driven content offerings, phygital art advisory services, and software services, we continued to strengthen our market position and open up new avenues for growth. We were also pleased with the success of our recent art exhibition and collector engagement, which highlighted the increasing value of connecting creators, audiences, and collectors through our ecosystem."

Mr. Li added, " Building on this foundation, including our recently completed art exhibition, we have begun generating revenue across art advisory, acquisition assistance, exhibition services, post-transaction support, and MCN brokerage services, and expect this momentum to continue. We are excited about what this means for our creator ecosystem, as these services have given creators a platform to showcase their work and a direct line to collectors who value their work. By broadening our services and deepening engagement with our community of creators and collectors, we believe we can further expand our market reach, scale our platform, and deliver sustainable, long-term value to our stockholders."

Stockholders’ deficit narrowed 34% from June 30. The Company converted $987,000 of accrued compensation to equity and appointed Brent Nelson as Chief Executive Officer

SOUTHLAKE, Texas, Nov. 13, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- American Fusion Inc. (OTCQB: AMFN) (“American Fusion” or the “Company”), developer of the proprietary Texatron™ Fusion Engine™, today announced the filing of its Quarterly Report on Form 10-Q for the quarter ended September 30, 2026. The Company also highlighted financial, operational and corporate progress during the quarter and in recent weeks.

During the third quarter, American Fusion strengthened its balance sheet and grew its intellectual property portfolio. It also invested in research and testing equipment and converted most of its accrued compensation obligations into long-term equity. After the quarter ended, the Company completed a leadership transition. It also raised additional capital as it prepares for the next phase of Texatron™ development and testing.

Third Quarter and Year-to-Date 2026 Financial Highlights

$1.55 million in financing year-to-date: Net cash provided by financing activities was $1,551,000 for the nine months ended September 30, 2026. This consisted of $1,071,000 from the Company’s fixed-price prepaid warrant facility and $480,000 from the sale of equity units to third-party investors at $0.05 to $0.07 per unit. Each unit included a warrant exercisable at $0.50 per share. Prepaid warrant funding in the third quarter alone totaled $446,000.

Total assets nearly doubled: Total assets increased to $372,313 at September 30, 2026, from $196,683 at June 30, 2026.

Liabilities reduced: Total liabilities declined approximately 21% to $1,473,333 at September 30, 2026, from $1,856,662 at June 30, 2026.

Stockholders’ deficit improved 34%: Total stockholders’ deficit improved to $(1,101,020) at September 30, 2026, from $(1,659,980) at June 30, 2026.

Patent portfolio expansion: Capitalized patent filing costs reached $166,992 for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, compared to $33,472 at June 30. This reflects a significant increase in new patent filings covering the Texatron™ platform.

Investment in testing infrastructure: The Company capitalized $44,169 of research and development testing equipment acquired for future projects.

Continued R&D investment: Research and development expense was $112,195 for the third quarter and $243,538 for the nine-month period.

Non-cash expense profile: Of the $1,399,778 in third quarter operating expenses, $764,752 (approximately 55%) was non-cash stock-based compensation, primarily for officer, director and advisory agreements.

Capital Structure and Governance

$986,958 of accrued compensation converted to equity: Effective September 30, 2026, twelve officers, directors, consultants and advisors agreed to exchange their rights to common stock compensation for newly designated Series C Convertible Preferred Stock. The exchange removed $986,958 of accrued compensation obligations and replaced them with equity. Series C shares generally cannot be converted into common stock until the later of full vesting and the earlier of (i) the 20th trading day after a national exchange listing or (ii) nine months after issuance. After that, conversions are spread over four quarters.

Share count held steady: Common shares outstanding were 1,619,034,363 at September 30, 2026. That is unchanged from June 30 and approximately 45% below the 2,954,801,029 shares outstanding at December 31, 2025. The reduction follows the court-ordered cancellation of 1.683 billion legacy shares earlier in the year.

Board strengthened: John Gerdin joined the Board of Directors on August 11, 2026. He brings board governance, corporate finance and capital markets experience.

Texas DSHS registration: On July 17, 2026, the Company received Certificate of Registration No. R54726 from the Texas Department of State Health Services. The registration covers twelve registered Texatron™ Fusion Engine™ research model classes ranging from 500 kW to 1 GW, for research and development activities at its authorized testing location in Lubbock, Texas. It remains effective through February 28, 2034. The registration authorizes research and development activities only and does not constitute certification of the Company’s technology or commercial performance.

Recent Developments

Leadership transition: On October 26, 2026, Brent Nelson, Executive Chairman since March 1, 2026, was appointed Chief Executive Officer and continues as Chairman of the Board. Richard C. Hawkins, the former Chief Executive Officer, was appointed Chief Administrative Officer.

Additional capital: In late October 2026, the Company received aggregate net financing of approximately $687,000 for the acquisition of a property for testing.

Independent technology review: As announced November 9, 2026, an independent third-party reviewer conducted an on-site evaluation of the Texatron™ platform. The Company anticipates receiving the reviewer’s final report before the end of November 2026.

North Texas facilities: The Company expects to complete the acquisition of its planned North Texas Ranch Facility before November 26, 2026, subject to customary closing requirements. Its previously executed factory and office leases are expected to commence in November 2026.

Proposed Restructuring of Consulting Notes

American Fusion is developing a proposed exchange of certain existing consulting-related notes associated with Pinnacle Consulting Services Inc. and CMB Communications for a new class of Series D Convertible Preferred Stock.

The proposed exchange is intended to replace the applicable debt obligations with equity. Completion remains subject to reconciliation of the outstanding note balances and prior assignments, execution of definitive agreements, and receipt of required corporate approvals.

Management Commentary

“The third quarter was about building a stronger foundation,” said Brent Nelson, Chairman and CEO of American Fusion. “We meaningfully expanded our patent portfolio, invested in testing equipment and moved nearly $1 million of accrued compensation off our balance sheet and into long-term equity. That equity is aligned with the success of our shareholders. Our stockholders’ deficit improved by roughly a third in a single quarter.”

“With the independent technology review underway, our Texas registration in place and our North Texas facilities coming online, we are focused on disciplined execution and transparent reporting as we advance the Texatron™ program,” Nelson continued.

Third Quarter 2026 Highlights

  • Revenue from new business accounted for 14% of net revenue

  • Digital revenue accounted for 23% of net revenue, or 24% of net revenue, excluding political  
  • Digital segment operating margin was 32%, up from 21% in Q3'25

During the third quarter of 2026, Beasley continued to advance its strategic priorities of rebuilding core revenue, expanding digital profitability, and strengthening its balance sheet through disciplined deleveraging and portfolio optimization. Building on the comprehensive debt restructuring completed in May, the Company raised gross proceeds of approximately $4.6 million through a registered direct offering and concurrent private placement in September. Subsequent to quarter-end, Beasley completed the sale of two radio stations and two parcels of real estate, generating more than $10 million in net proceeds for the four assets sold. These actions further strengthened the Company's financial position, reducing the outstanding principal amount of first-lien notes to approximately $3.6 million and providing additional flexibility to execute its long-term operating strategy.

Net revenue during the three months ended September 30, 2026 of $42.8 million decreased 16.1%, or 10.2% on a same-station basis, reflecting continued weakness in traditional national and local agency advertising. These declines were partially offset by a 7% increase in local direct revenue on a same-station basis and contributions from political advertising. Digital revenue declined 12.3% on a same-station basis during the quarter, although year-to-date same-station digital revenue increased 4.4%. Importantly, digital operating margins expanded to approximately 32%, compared with 21% (or 26% on a same-station basis) in the prior-year period, reflecting continued progress toward a more efficient, higher-margin digital business.

Operating expenses, excluding corporate expenses, depreciation and amortization, declined approximately $7.0 million, or 15.1% year-over-year, reflecting the continued benefits of structural cost reduction initiatives implemented over the past two years. On a same-station basis, operating expenses declined approximately $3.7 million. The third quarter reflected a more complete benefit from the Company's most recent expense reduction initiatives implemented in May 2026, demonstrating the ongoing impact of its efforts to establish a more efficient and sustainable operating model.

Station Operating Income totaled approximately $3.6 million, representing an SOI margin of 8.5%. Corporate expenses totaled approximately $3.9 million, compared with $2.2 million in the prior-year period, reflecting restructuring, financing, and strategic transaction-related costs, as well as the absence of a prior-year franchise tax benefit. Excluding applicable nonrecurring items, corporate expenses were approximately $2.8 million.

Adjusted EBITDA was approximately $1.3 million for the third quarter of 2026, compared with $3.9 million in the prior-year period. While profitability continued to reflect pressure from lower advertising revenue, the Company's structural expense reductions meaningfully reduced the impact on operating performance.

Commenting on the financial results, Caroline Beasley, Chief Executive Officer, said:

"While the advertising environment remains challenging, our third-quarter results demonstrate the tangible progress we are making in building a more efficient and financially resilient company. The structural cost reductions implemented over the past two years are helping us protect profitability amid continued revenue pressure, while our digital business is generating stronger operating margins. We are encouraged by the growth in local direct advertising and remain focused on rebuilding revenue, improving sales productivity, and expanding the higher-margin products and services that we believe will support sustainable growth." 

"Looking ahead, our priorities remain clear: stabilize and rebuild core revenue, expand digital profitability, improve free cash flow generation, and continue reducing leverage. While there is more work ahead, we believe the actions we have taken have established a stronger operating and financial foundation. As we enter the next phase of our transformation, we remain focused on translating these improvements into more consistent financial performance and creating long-term value for our stockholders."

Conference Call and Webcast Information

The Company will host a conference call and webcast today, November 13, 2026 at 4:30 p.m. ET to discuss its financial results and operations. To access the conference call, interested parties may dial (800) 715-9871 or +1 (646) 307-1963 conference ID 1613596 (domestic and international callers). Participants can also listen to a live webcast of the call at the Company's website at www.bbgi.com. Please allow 15 minutes to register and download and install any necessary software. Following its completion, a replay of the webcast can be accessed for five days on the Company's website, www.bbgi.com.

Questions from analysts, institutional investors and debt holders may be e-mailed to ir@bbgi.com at any time up until 2:30 p.m. ET on Friday, November 13, 2026. Management will answer as many questions as possible during the conference call and webcast (provided the questions are not addressed in their prepared remarks).

About Beasley Broadcast Group

The Company is a multi-platform media company whose primary business is operating radio stations throughout the United States. The Company offers local and national advertisers integrated marketing solutions across audio, digital and event platforms. The Company owns and operates 47 AM and FM stations in the following large- and mid-size markets in the United States: Augusta, GA, Boston, MA, Charlotte, NC, Detroit, MI, Fayetteville, NC, Las Vegas, NV, Middlesex, NJ, Monmouth, NJ, Morristown, NJ, Philadelphia, PA, and Tampa-Saint Petersburg, FL. Approximately 17 million consumers listen to the Company's radio stations weekly over-the-air, online and on smartphones and tablets, and millions regularly engage with the Company's brands and personalities through digital platforms such as Facebook, X, text, apps and email. For more information, please visit www.bbgi.com. 

For further information, or to receive future Beasley Broadcast Group news announcements via e-mail, please contact Beasley Broadcast Group, at 239-263-5000 or ir@bbgi.com. 

Definitions

EBITDA is defined as net income (loss) before interest income or expense, income tax expense or benefit, depreciation, and amortization.    

Adjusted EBITDA is defined as EBITDA further adjusted to exclude certain non-operating or other items that we believe are not indicative of the performance of our ongoing operations, such as impairment losses, other income or expense, one-time severance expense, stock-based compensation or equity in earnings of unconsolidated affiliates, gains on dispositions and gain on debt restructure. See "Reconciliation of Net Income (Loss) to Adjusted EBITDA" for additional information.      

Adjusted EBITDA is a measure widely used in the media industry. The Company recognizes that because Adjusted EBITDA is not calculated in accordance with GAAP, it is not necessarily comparable to similarly titled measures employed by other companies. However, management believes that Adjusted EBITDA provides meaningful information to investors because it is an important measure of how effectively we operate our business and assists investors in comparing our operating performance with that of other media companies. 

Same station revenue and same station operating expenses exclude revenue or operating expenses, as applicable, from all divestitures and other operations that were exited in the prior 12 months. These measures provide investors with a clearer view of core business performance by eliminating the impact of portfolio changes and enabling more meaningful year-over-year comparisons. By isolating the performance of continuing operations, same station results offer greater transparency into underlying trends, operational execution, and the effectiveness of strategic initiative. 

New business revenue is defined as revenue from an advertiser that has not advertised in the prior 13 months before the start of the current quarter.

CENTENNIAL, CO / ACCESS Newswire / November 13, 2026 / NioCorp Developments Ltd. ("NioCorp," "our," or the "Company") (NASDAQ:NB), a leading U.S. critical minerals developer, is pleased to announce that the Export-Import Bank of the United States ("EXIM") has featured the Company's Elk Creek Critical Minerals Project (the "Elk Creek Project") in southeast Nebraska as part of EXIM's Factory Floor Fridays initiative, highlighting the pivotal role Elk Creek will prospectively play in strengthening domestic critical mineral supply chains and supporting American manufacturing.

Through its Factory Floor Fridays initiative, EXIM showcases American companies and workers contributing to the next generation of U.S. industry, including projects aimed at strengthening domestic production, supporting American jobs, and improving the competitiveness of U.S. manufacturers.

"EXIM is proud to support projects like NioCorp's Elk Creek mine that will unlock domestic mineral resources, create well-paying jobs, and provide an important boost to reindustrializing America," said John Jovanovic, EXIM Chairman.

"The decision by EXIM to showcase the Elk Creek Project speaks to the growing recognition that America needs to develop its own sources of the critical minerals essential to our economy and national security," said Mark A. Smith, NioCorp Executive Chairman and CEO. "Chairman Jovanovic and his team understand what it takes to bring projects of this scale into production, and we greatly appreciate their continued support. Our focus remains on completing the financing process and bringing this important source of American critical minerals into production as quickly as possible."

The feature includes a video highlighting EXIM Chairman and President John Jovanovic's October 14, 2026 visit to the Elk Creek Project, where he was joined by U.S. Secretary of Energy Chris Wright, Nebraska Governor Jim Pillen, U.S. Senators Deb Fischer and Pete Ricketts, U.S. Representative Adrian Smith, Nebraska Senator Bob Hallstrom, other state and local leaders, and NioCorp leadership.

During the visit, Chairman Jovanovic and NioCorp Executive Chairman and CEO Mark A. Smith signed a Letter of Support (the "Letter") in which EXIM reiterated its target of providing debt financing equivalent to approximately 65% of the Project's upfront capital expenditures, subject to applicable financing requirements and satisfactory completion of EXIM's due diligence and approval processes. The Letter also indicated that EXIM expects to continue advancing its due diligence efforts toward further internal review through its Transaction Review Committee process as expeditiously as practicable.

The Elk Creek Project is designed to produce niobium, scandium, titanium and several rare earth products from a single ore body in southeast Nebraska. These materials are critical to U.S. defense, aerospace, automotive, energy security and advanced manufacturing supply chains, with the United States currently heavily reliant on imports for almost all of these minerals.

EXIM's Factory Floor Fridays feature, including video footage from Chairman Jovanovic's visit to the Elk Creek Project, is available here: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=51AUHDZCQp0.

ABOUT NIOCORP

NioCorp is developing the Elk Creek Project that is expected to produce niobium, scandium, titanium and several rare earth products, including neodymium-praseodymium oxide, dysprosium oxide, terbium oxide, samarium-europium-gadolinium ("SEG") carbonate, and heavy rare earth carbonate. Niobium is used to produce specialty alloys as well as High Strength, Low Alloy steel, which is a lighter, stronger steel used in automotive, structural, and pipeline applications. Scandium is a specialty metal that can be combined with Aluminum to make alloys with increased strength and improved corrosion resistance. Scandium is also a critical component of advanced solid oxide fuel cells. Titanium is used in various lightweight alloys and is a key component of pigments used in paper, paint and plastics and is also used for aerospace applications, armor, and medical implants. Magnetic rare earths, such as neodymium, praseodymium, terbium, and dysprosium are critical to the making of neodymium-iron-boron magnets, which are used across a wide variety of defense and civilian applications.

PITTSBURGH--(BUSINESS WIRE)-- Today, the Federal Home Loan Bank of Pittsburgh (FHLBank) joined Rebuilding Together Pittsburgh (RTP) alongside U.S. Rep. Summer Lee (D-PA-12), First Commonwealth Bank and stakeholders at a ribbon cutting for two Rehab for Resale (R4R) properties, located at 205 and 207 Rankin Blvd., as part of the Mon Valley Phase IV initiative.

In 2024-2025, FHLBank awarded nearly $5.7 million in Affordable Housing Program (AHP) and Voluntary Housing Grant (VHG) funding through its member financial institution, First Commonwealth Bank, to support RTP’s important rehabilitation efforts providing affordable homeownership opportunities throughout Mon Valley communities.

R4R Mon Valley Phase IV is an installment of a collaborative initiative between RTP, the Tri-COG Land Bank and First Commonwealth Bank to expand access to affordable homeownership in a region facing significant housing challenges.

“Increased access to quality, affordable housing is a core outcome of FHLBank’s dual mission,” said David G. Paulson, FHLBank president and CEO. “We are proud to support this initiative through multiple funding rounds of our Community Investment Products and are encouraged by the strong regional partnerships formed to not only preserve the existing housing supply, but also to create long-term wealth building opportunities and brighter futures for the families that will live here.”

The townhomes toured by event attendees today were two among six formerly vacant and blighted structures that Rebuilding Together Pittsburgh identified as opportunities to be restored into safe, healthy and affordable homes designated for buyers earning equal to or less than 80% of the area median income.

“We’re deeply grateful to FHLBank and our member bank, First Commonwealth Bank, for this partnership,” said Travis Renville, CEO, Rebuilding Together Pittsburgh. “Their support helps homeowners remain safely in the homes and communities they know and love, while allowing us to bring vacant homes back into use as safe, stable, and affordable places for new homeowners. By reducing blight, returning homes to the tax rolls, and welcoming new neighbors, this work helps strengthen communities in lasting ways.”

“We've got families across the Mon Valley who want to own a home, raise their kids, and build a future right here, but too often, the cost of housing puts that dream out of reach. Meanwhile, we've got vacant houses sitting in neighborhoods that deserve investment and a chance to thrive,” said Rep. Summer Lee. “I love seeing partners come together to give these homes new life and help working families build stability and generational wealth. I'm grateful to RTP, FHLBank, First Commonwealth Bank and everyone who helped make this happen, and I'm excited to see more of our neighbors get the opportunity to become homeowners.”

About FHLBank Pittsburgh

FHLBank Pittsburgh provides reliable funding and liquidity to its member financial institutions, which include commercial and savings banks, community development financial institutions, credit unions and insurance companies in Delaware, Pennsylvania and West Virginia. FHLBank products and resources help support community lending, housing and economic development. As one of 11 Federal Home Loan Banks established by Congress, FHLBank has been an integral and reliable part of the financial system since 1932. Learn more by visiting www.fhlb-pgh.com.

About Rebuilding Together Pittsburgh

Rebuilding Together Pittsburgh works to ensure everyone can live in a safe, healthy home. Since 1993, RTP has provided critical repairs for low- and moderate-income homeowners across the Pittsburgh region, helping residents remain safely housed, preserving affordable homeownership, and preventing homes from becoming vacant or blighted. Through its Rehab for Resale program, RTP also rehabilitates vacant homes and makes them affordable for income-qualified buyers, returning neglected properties to productive use and strengthening neighborhoods.

About First Commonwealth Financial Corporation

First Commonwealth Financial Corporation (NYSE: FCF), headquartered in Indiana, Pennsylvania, is a community bank committed to its mission of improving the financial lives of its neighbors and their businesses. First Commonwealth operates 126 branches throughout Pennsylvania and Ohio and also has business banking centers in Pittsburgh and Harrisburg, Pennsylvania; and Cleveland, Canton, Cincinnati and Columbus, Ohio. First Commonwealth, through subsidiaries First Commonwealth Bank and First Commonwealth Insurance Agency, provides a full range of commercial and retail banking services, including mortgage, wealth management and insurance solutions, along with equipment financing and SBA and indirect lending. For more information about First Commonwealth, visit www.fcbanking.com.

STOCKTON, Calif., Nov. 12, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Health Net, one of California's most experienced Medi-Cal managed care health plans and company of Centene Corporation (NYSE: CNC), today announced a $3 million investment in the San Joaquin Regional Housing Fund. The funding will provide grants and low-interest loans to accelerate affordable housing developments and support the creation of at least 75 affordable homes for Stockton families facing some of the region's most significant housing challenges.

"A home is so much more than a roof overhead. It's the place where families feel safe, children can grow and learn, and people can focus on their health and well-being," said Dorothy M. Seleski, Medi-Cal Plan President at Health Net. "Too many families in our communities are struggling to find housing they can afford. By partnering with the San Joaquin Regional Housing Fund, we're helping create more opportunities for families to put down roots, build stability and look toward the future with greater confidence. Together, we're investing in healthier communities by helping more people find a place to call home."

The investment will support community-driven housing developments, with a focus on serving families facing the greatest barriers to affordable housing, including households earning between 30% and 50% of the area median income.

"When local organizations unite around a shared goal, communities move forward," said San Joaquin Regional Housing Fund Board Chair Gary Singh. "Health Net's investment will help transform plans into homes for local families while encouraging broader community participation in addressing the region's housing needs."

The investment will support eligible projects through January 2029, from planning through construction.

"Investments in affordable housing are investments in the health, strength and future of our communities," said San Joaquin County Supervisor Robert Rickman. "By bringing public, private and community partners together, we can help more San Joaquin County families find stable housing and create lasting opportunity across the region."

In Sacramento and San Joaquin counties, Health Net has invested a combined $11 million in affordable housing and related initiatives, including $2 million to Stanislaus Equity Partners, Inc. (STEP) and $3 million to Fairview Terrace. By supporting developments at every stage, from planning and financing to construction and occupancy, Health Net is helping expand access to affordable housing, strengthen local communities and create the conditions for better health across the region.

Founded in California more than 45 years ago, Health Net, LLC ("Health Net"), a company of Centene Corporation, believes that every person deserves a safety net for their health, regardless of age, income, employment status or current state of health. Today, we provide health plans for individuals, families, businesses of every size and people who qualify for Medi-Cal or Medicare. With more than 117,000 of our network providers, Health Net serves more than three million members across the state. We also offer access to substance abuse programs, behavioral health services and managed healthcare products related to prescription drugs. We make these health plans and services available through Health Net and its subsidiaries: Health Net of California, Inc., Health Net Life Insurance Company and Health Net Community Solutions, Inc. These entities are wholly owned subsidiaries of Centene Corporation (NYSE: CNC), a leading healthcare enterprise committed to transforming the health of the communities we serve, one person at a time. Health Net and Centene Corporation employ more than 5,700 people in California who work at one of five regional Talent Hub offices. For more information, visit www.HealthNet.com.
